en.page_title: Case Study: OpenCart 1.5 to 3.0 Migration - Bowei Xu
en.page_description: How I migrated a live store from OpenCart 1.5.6.4 to 3.0.3.8: 2,000+ products and 70,000+ orders, reconciled table by table, with no business interruption.
en.title: E-Commerce Platform Upgrade (OpenCart 1.5 to 3.0)
en.disclaimer: A sanitized write-up of the e-commerce platform upgrade I led as the sole developer at Fuel Cell Store. Product details and proprietary code are omitted. It describes the approach and engineering decisions only.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The online store ran on OpenCart 1.5, two major versions behind the 3.x line it needed to reach, with no supported upgrade path. Custom modules and theme changes had accumulated on top of the core over several years with no documentation, so the behavior of much of the custom functionality was effectively unknown.
With no reliable automated path across that version gap, the project combined reverse engineering, data migration, and the rebuilding of custom functionality in roughly equal measure.

architecture.host: cPanel/WHM VPS, separate from the ERP server

tiers.label: OpenCart 3.0.3.8 on PHP 7.4
items: online quote and request for quote

architecture.aria: Architecture diagram: the browser talks over HTTPS to a cPanel/WHM VPS, separate from the ERP server, running OpenCart 3.0.3.8 on PHP 7.4 backed by MySQL.

sections.heading: Approach
paragraphs: The gap between the two versions is a set of breaking changes rather than an increment. The template engine moves from native PHP files to Twig, the extension system from vQmod to OCMod, the directory layout is reorganized, and a number of database tables are restructured. A direct in-place upgrade was not viable, so I approached it as a rebuild on the new version paired with a controlled data migration, developed and rehearsed on a staging copy before any production cutover.
list: Set up a clean target-version installation on staging
Audit the legacy store feature by feature, directly from its code
For each feature, adopt a maintained extension or build a custom one
Write SQL scripts to clean and remap the legacy data into the new schema
Rebuild the theme and re-implement admin customizations
Reconcile the migrated data, then cut over to production

subsections.title: 1. Reverse engineering features with no documentation
subsections.body: The store carried years of undocumented customization. I read the legacy controllers, models, and template overrides to reconstruct what each feature actually did before deciding how to rebuild it. This ensured that behavior the business depended on was not inadvertently lost.

subsections.title: 2. Adopt or build, without editing the core
subsections.body: For each legacy module I made an explicit decision: adopt a maintained extension where a reliable one existed, or build a custom one where it did not. In both cases the changes were applied through the platform's modification system rather than by editing core files, so customizations sit on top of the core and the store remains upgradeable rather than being locked to a single version again.

subsections.title: 3. Cross-version data migration in hand-written SQL
subsections.body: The two schemas differ in table layout and relationships, so I wrote SQL scripts to clean, map, and rebuild the data rather than relying on an automated importer. Relational data such as product accessories, SEO URLs, and zone-to-geo-zone mappings had to be remapped table by table to fit the new structure.

subsections.title: 4. Reconciling the migration before cutover
subsections.body: The entire migration was built and rehearsed on a staging copy of the live store, and nothing moved to production until the copy reconciled against the source three ways: row counts table by table, summed order totals, and manual spot-checks on sampled records. The catalog is what made the third pass necessary. Products carry multi-dimension variants with their own price, SKU, weight, and stock per combination, and part of the catalog sells through a quote-only path rather than through checkout, so a mismatch that counts and totals both clear would surface later as a wrong price or an unsellable product. Order IDs were carried across unchanged rather than renumbered, so the order references customers and the support team already held stayed valid. The production cutover was completed with no business downtime.

subsections.title: 5. Rebuilding the templates by hand
subsections.body: The old templates are native PHP and the new ones are Twig, and the data passed into them changed shape at the same time. A conversion script would have left every file to be corrected by hand anyway, and the number of customized templates sat below the point where writing one would pay for itself, so I rebuilt them individually. Each one meant working out what the customization depended on in the old engine before reimplementing it on the new one. Mobile responsiveness was improved in the process. On the admin side, customizations and third-party module compatibility were re-implemented so the team's daily workflows continued without interruption.

sections.heading: Results
list: Upgraded the store from 1.5.6.4 to 3.0.3.8 across 2,000+ products and 70,000+ historical orders, reconciled table by table, with order volume holding steady through the rebuild and the cutover
Carried order IDs across unchanged rather than renumbering, so the order references customers and the support team already held stayed valid after the cutover

Rewrote the store's custom features on 3.0 instead of porting the old code, preserving existing behavior such as standard checkout, the quote-only flow, and per-combination variant pricing and stock, while fixing legacy bugs and adding new functionality
Reconstructed and re-implemented years of undocumented custom functionality by reading the legacy code
Migrated customizations onto the modification system, so the store no longer depends on edited core files and can be updated more safely

zh.page_title: 案例研究：OpenCart 1.5 到 3.0 迁移 - 徐博伟
zh.page_description: 我如何将线上商店从 OpenCart 1.5.6.4 迁移到 3.0.3.8：2000 多个商品、7 万多条历史订单，逐表对账，业务不中断。
zh.title: 电商平台升级（OpenCart 1.5 到 3.0）
zh.disclaimer: 这是一份脱敏的案例分析。我作为唯一开发者，在 Fuel Cell Store 主导了这次电商平台升级。产品细节和专有代码均已省略，此处仅描述思路与工程决策。

sections.heading: 背景
paragraphs: 在线商城运行在 OpenCart 1.5 上，落后目标的 3.x 两个大版本，且没有受支持的升级路径。多年间，自定义模块和主题改动持续叠加在核心之上，没有任何文档，大量自定义功能的具体实现无从查起。
跨大版本又无可靠的自动化路径，这项工作主要由逆向分析、数据迁移和重建自定义功能三部分大致均衡地构成。

architecture.host: cPanel/WHM VPS，与 ERP 服务器彼此独立

tiers.label: OpenCart 3.0.3.8，PHP 7.4
items: 商品目录、购物车与结账

architecture.aria: 架构图：浏览器通过 HTTPS 访问一台 cPanel/WHM VPS，该服务器与 ERP 服务器彼此独立，运行 OpenCart 3.0.3.8（PHP 7.4），数据存于 MySQL。

sections.heading: 迁移思路
paragraphs: 两个版本之间是一组破坏性变更，而不是一次增量升级。模板引擎从原生 PHP 文件换成 Twig，扩展机制从 vQmod 换成 OCMod，目录结构重新组织，若干数据库表的结构也发生了变化。原地直接升级并不可行，因此我将其作为在新版本上的重建来处理，并配以一套受控的数据迁移，全部先在 staging 副本上搭建与演练，确认无误后再切至生产。
list: 在 staging 上搭建一个干净的目标版本环境
对照旧代码，逐一梳理旧商城的各项功能
对每个功能，采用成熟扩展或自行实现
编写 SQL 脚本，清洗并将旧数据重映射到新库结构
重建主题，重做后台自定义功能
对账迁移后的数据，再切换至生产

subsections.title: 1. 在无文档情况下逆向功能
subsections.body: 商城积累了多年的自定义改动，没有任何文档。我通过阅读旧的控制器、模型和模板覆盖，先还原每个功能的实际行为，再决定如何重建，以确保不会遗漏业务实际依赖的功能。

subsections.title: 2. 采用或自建，但均不改动核心
subsections.body: 对每个旧模块，我都做出明确取舍：有可靠的成熟扩展则采用，否则自行实现。两种情况下，改动都通过平台的修改机制叠加，而非直接修改核心文件，因此自定义改动叠加在核心之上，商城保持可升级，而不会再次被锁定在某个特定版本。

subsections.title: 3. 以手写 SQL 完成跨版本数据迁移
subsections.body: 新旧两套库在表结构和关联关系上均不相同，因此我编写 SQL 脚本来清洗、映射并重建数据，而非依赖自动导入工具。商品配件、SEO URL、区域到地理区域映射等关联数据，需逐表重新映射，才能适配新结构。

subsections.title: 4. 切换前的数据对账
subsections.body: 整个迁移都在生产商城的 staging 副本上搭建与演练，副本必须通过三道对账才允许切到生产：逐表核对记录总数、汇总订单金额、以及对抽样记录做人工核对。第三道是目录逼出来的。商品带多维度规格，每个规格组合有各自的价格、SKU、重量和库存，目录中还有一部分商品走的是仅报价路径而非标准结账，因此前两道都能放行的错位，会在日后表现为价格错误或商品不可售。订单号原样保留，没有重新编号，因此客户和客服手上已有的订单号在切换后依然有效。切换至生产时业务零停机。

subsections.title: 5. 手工逐个重建模板
subsections.body: 旧模板是原生 PHP，新模板是 Twig，与此同时传入模板的数据结构也变了。写转换脚本，转出来的东西仍然要逐个手工修正，而被定制过的模板数量还够不上写转换器的划算阈值，所以我选择逐个重建。每一个都要先弄清这处定制在旧引擎里依赖什么，再在新引擎上重新实现一遍。移动端适配在这个过程中一并提升。后台方面，自定义功能与第三方模块兼容性同样经过重做，使团队的日常流程不中断地继续运转。

sections.heading: 成果
list: 将商城从 1.5.6.4 升级至 3.0.3.8，覆盖 2,000+ 商品和 70,000+ 历史订单，逐表对账，订单量在整个重建与切换期间保持平稳
订单号原样保留而非重新编号，客户和客服手上已有的订单号在切换后依然有效
在 3.0 上重写商城的定制功能，而非移植旧代码，尽量保留原有行为（标准结账、仅报价流程、按规格组合设定的价格和库存），同时修复遗留 bug 并新增功能
通过阅读旧代码，还原并重做了多年积累的、无文档的自定义功能
将自定义改动迁移至修改机制之上，商城不再依赖被修改的核心文件，今后可更安全地升级
